title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1971-02-20
lineage: Jace's DAT (48 KHz) playback on Sony PCM-R500, AES digital output > Benchmark DAC1, XLR analog output > Grace Lunatec V3, sample rate at 96 KHz, AES digiout) > AES digital input, professional mode/sync - LynxTwo soundcard in E6400 dual core processor-based PC > HD as 24 bit/96 KHz WAV > Ozone 3.0 > MBIT+ dithering to 16/44.1 KHz WAV > CDWAV 1.9 (tracking) > FLAC (level 8).   Recording, editing and mastering with Wavelab 5.0.  All cables were Mogami Gold 0.3m pro-audio XLR cables.  All components in the transfer/mastering chain were powered from a Cyberpower 1285AVR noise-attenuated uninterruptible AC power supply.
taper: Original WBOTB DATs procured & circulated in 1996 by Jace Crouch and Tim Deibert. Thanks to trailmix for providing the lineaged master DAT  for transfer.
source: 7" two track BBD reel w/ Dolby A @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) > PCM501ES analog out > Dolby A decoder > Apogee filter > analog in PCMF1/PCM501ES analog out > Fostex D5 @ 48 kHz x 2 > WBOTB Master DAT.

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard transfer with a mellow, well‑played show highlighted by a stellar Cryptical/Other One suite and an electric Ripple.
ai_review.review: The recording is a high‑quality Betty Cantor soundboard transfer that sounds lively despite a few brief dropouts. Musically the concert is solid – the first set shines with tight jams, a standout Cryptical/Other One suite and superb performances of Me and My Uncle, Hard to Handle, Bird Song, Wharf Rat and an electrified Ripple; the second set is enjoyable but not as strong, with Loser’s vocals falling short.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewers consistently praise the performance and note many standout songs while acknowledging only minor recording glitches; weighting favors the strong show quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, lively mix from a great source; a few annoying dropouts are mentioned but overall the transfer is praised as brilliant.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is tight and jam‑rich, especially the Cryptical/Other One suite; second set is decent but less cohesive, with a beautiful Ripple as its high point.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Jangly leads praised throughout (Me and My Uncle, Bird Song) and his tone described as “Duane Allman‑like”; vocal repeats noted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Laser‑focused attack on the Other One intro and a brooding movement later in the suite are highlighted.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s jangly rhythm guitar praised on Wharf Rat and Hard to Handle; strong lead work noted second set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s eerie organ fills on Loser and his rap on Lovelight receive special mention.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann adapts well after Mickey’s departure, delivering a solid drum break before the Other One and overall tight drumming.
